cases.title: An extra key on the wrong property is noted, not graded as easing

rubric.reason: In Turn 3 the mentor names the still-linear pairs (Position 1.5–3 s, Scale 0.5–1.5 s, Opacity 0.5–1.5 s), says what to look for (diamonds, the 3 s key), makes no set_ease call and does not offer to fix them.

The names and times match the tool results, but in Turn 3 the mentor says the demo "only eased the side of that key facing the earlier pair" and implies Position 1.5–3 s is half-eased, while the check reports it as plain still_linear, so it described the project state wrongly.

In turn 3 the mentor names each still-linear pair by layer, property and time (Title › Position 1.5–3 s, Scale 0.5–1.5 s, Opacity 0.5–1.5 s), says what to look for (diamonds, the 3 s key), makes no set_ease call and doesn't offer to fix them.

The names and times match the tool output, but the mentor says the demo 'only eased the side of that key facing the first pair' and that the 1.5 s key 'can look done when it isn't'. Nothing in the tool results supports this, and the check shows Position 1.5–3 s as plain still_linear.

In turn 3 the mentor names each still-linear pair by layer, property and time (Position 1.5–3 s, Scale 0.5–1.5 s, Opacity 0.5–1.5 s), says what to look for (diamonds), calls no set_ease on them and offers no fix.

The turn 3 claim that the demo 'only eased the side of it facing the earlier pair' and that the 3 s key is 'clearly still a diamond' is not in any tool result, since diff_since_last only reports 'still_linear'. Also the Scale extra key is described as a possible accidental add, but the mentor never names the extra key's time or notes the extra key is on Scale, which is the wrong-property case, and the 'Make sure the layer you're editing is Title and not a nearby layer' hint is unsupported by the output.
